# Getting Started with GeoAI at Your Organization

Before writing any code, understand the strategic context you are operating in. Your organization's GeoAI strategy defines what you should build, what data you can use, and what governance gates you must pass.

## The Five-Question Filter: Your Strategic Sanity Check

Before writing a single line of code, confirm that your project has passed the organization's [GeoAI Decision Filter](../decision-makers/five-questions.qmd) — five sequential gates that separate validated use cases from innovation theater. If your project hasn't cleared these gates, you are building something that may never be used.

As a developer, here's what each gate means for your work:

| Gate | Strategic Question | What It Means for You |
|------|-------------------|----------------------|
| **Q1: The Filter** | Does location fundamentally change this decision? | If geography isn't load-bearing, you're building a map layer, not GeoAI. Push back. |
| **Q2: Data Position** | Do we have differentiated spatial data? | If the answer is "just Sentinel-2 and census data," your model outputs will be commodity. Raise this early. |
| **Q3: Tempo** | What decision latency must this serve? | This determines your entire architecture — batch pipeline vs. streaming vs. edge. Get this wrong and you rebuild from scratch. |
| **Q4: Adoption** | Who will act on this, and do they trust it? | If no one can name the end user, your model will sit on a shelf. Insist on meeting the person who will use your output. |
| **Q5: Error Budget** | What's the cost of being wrong spatially? | This sets your evaluation rigor, human review requirements, and monitoring investment. A Tier 4 (safety) use case requires every technique in the [Evaluation chapter](evaluation.qmd). |

::: {.callout-warning}
## When to Push Back
If you're asked to start a project and leadership can't answer these five questions, that is a red flag — not a "we'll figure it out later" situation. Building a model for an unvalidated use case is the most expensive way to discover it was the wrong project. Raise the gap before you write code, not after.
:::

## Understanding Your Organization's GeoAI Strategy

::: {.callout-tip}
## Alignment Point
Your organization's GeoAI strategy is defined in the [Decision Maker Playbook — Strategy](../decision-makers/strategy.qmd) chapter. Read it before starting a new project.
:::

Before beginning any GeoAI project, answer these questions:

1. **What is the approved use case?** — Confirm your project aligns with the organizational strategy and Acceptable Use Policy.
2. **What data am I authorized to use?** — Check the data catalog and licensing constraints.
3. **What governance gates must I pass?** — Know the review requirements before you start, not after.
4. **Who are my stakeholders?** — Identify the Model Owner, domain experts, and governance reviewers.
5. **What does "done" look like?** — Understand the success metrics defined in the strategy.

## Your Role in the GeoAI Team

Depending on your organization's team structure, you may fill one or more of these roles:

| Role | Primary Responsibilities |
|------|------------------------|
| **GeoAI Engineer** | Model development, training, evaluation |
| **Data Engineer** | Data pipelines, ETL, catalog management |
| **MLOps Engineer** | Deployment, monitoring, infrastructure |
| **Domain Specialist** | Requirements, validation, interpretation |

## Setting Up Your Development Environment

### Prerequisites

```bash
# Python environment (3.10+)
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Core geospatial + ML dependencies
pip install rasterio geopandas shapely pyproj
pip install torch torchvision  # or tensorflow
pip install scikit-learn xgboost

# Data discovery and access
pip install pystac-client planetary-computer

# MLOps and experiment tracking
pip install mlflow dvc
```

### Project Structure Convention

```
my-geoai-project/
├── data/
│   ├── raw/              # Original, immutable data
│   ├── processed/        # Cleaned and transformed data
│   └── catalog.yml       # Data catalog entries
├── models/
│   ├── training/         # Training scripts
│   ├── evaluation/       # Evaluation scripts and results
│   └── cards/            # Model cards
├── pipelines/            # Data and ML pipelines
├── notebooks/            # Exploratory notebooks
├── tests/                # Unit and integration tests
└── README.md
```

## Checklist: Before You Start a New Project

- [ ] Reviewed organizational GeoAI strategy
- [ ] Confirmed use case is covered by the Acceptable Use Policy
- [ ] Identified data sources and confirmed access authorization
- [ ] Opened a Model Intake request (see shared procedure: model-intake)
- [ ] Set up project repository following the structure convention
- [ ] Identified governance reviewer and scheduled initial consultation
